FATHER SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK No. 2
Pg. 45 salvation. His one condition is, "Come to me -
cont. and I will refresh you." The bread that I will give is my flesh for the life of the world." "Not as your fathers did eat manna in the desert and are dead; he that eateth this bread shall live for ever." The eternal desire of Jesus to be one with us - little children, He expresses as He is about to insitute the Sacrament of love. "With desire I have desired to eat this ---. And speak- ing of Holy Communion, Leo XIII --- "with desire He desireth this singular mode of union with men. " To bring men to Jesus in any great numbers we must begin with them as little children -- Then remember the purpose of Holy Communion. It is a preservative against mortal sin and a medicine - daily faults.
Pg. 46 (Ist for Feast of the Sm Cordis 1917 not used. ) "Behold the Heart that has loved Men so much!" If in regard to men the saying is true that "familiarity begets contempt" it can never truly be said in regard to Almighty God. On the contrary, the more we learn to know of His divine Majesty, the more we are drawn to rev- erence Him, to love Him, to adore Him. The more thoroughly we understand any of His works, the more we must admire the wisdom of the Creator till with St. Paul (Rom. XI) we exclaim in utter astonishment "O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incompre- hensible are His judgments and how unsearchable His ways !"
Pg. 47 5th Sunday of P. Epiph. Nov. 11, '17 10 1/4 A.M. And the servants said to him, wilt thou that we go and gather it up? And he said no: "Matt. 13 If we but reflect for a moment on the mission that Jesus came among men to fulfill, we may be sure that His words were always earnest and solemn. Though His smile was ravishingly sweet He never laughed. The parables which He brought forth, as e.g. the one in Todays lesson, breathe themselves a decided solemn earnestness: This especially when we go a little further on in the same XIII chapter of St. Matt. where He deigns to explain this parable to His disciples, concluding with these words, "Even as cockle therefore is gathered up and burnt with fire: so shall it be at the end of the world. The Son of man shall
